nextRuntime.scope: Package name/version and CLI entrypoint bytes only; transitive dependency integrity is not established.

discovery.reviewer: Root (Claude Code), source review of the turn-6 snapshot plus a disposable scratch build read with the measurement text walker
discovery.scope: The single story route with all ten beats of the approved storyboard; the selected Opening A and Closing A as whole beats; in-beat contact, CV, project and same-story links; the Mosslink page, HTML CV as page and download, the 404, share image, icon, the wording decision archive and the concept archive. Header, chapter and footer navigation are covered by the raw control census, not listed as required links.

eligibility.rationale: The turn-6 closure-time snapshot holds the authored nested site with all ten beats, the custom fixture geometry and the auxiliary pages. This is eligibility for measurement, not a pass.

requiredText: 1 / Prepare Ada Mensah / Embedded firmware Code meets the bench. I’m Ada Mensah. I’m looking for embedded firmware roles involving physical devices. For Mosslink, an environmental sensor, I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture. How does a firmware decision become something you can check? Inspect the fixture ↓ Evidence & contact Download HTML CV Firmware is the code that controls a physical device’s operation. Bring-up means checking a new board’s basic operation.

5 / Record The claim follows the observation. A firmware decision needs a physical observation. An estimate and an observed run support different claims. That is the lesson I want to bring to firmware work involving physical devices. A current trace showed the radio staying awake after a failed transmission. No cause, fix, timing or later resolution is confirmed. No trace file is available to publish. ada@example.com ↗ View / print CV Download HTML CV ↓ Read the Mosslink project Back to the start ↑

limits: Ten beats under the author's prospective ten-beat exception; the frozen policy's 12-to-22 count still reports a scope problem, which is expected and not waived.
Built with STORYFOLIO_DIST_DIR=.next under the author's decision; the agent's own default build folder is .next-concepts.
The three /sketch concept studies are not separately covered.
Headless software rendering does not prove physical-phone performance or visual quality; every original needs human review.

policy.focusOnlyAllowance: At most one source-bound document-start skip to the main story; actual sequential-Tab focus and target response remain required.
limits: No automatic material-look, semantic, full-journey or author-acceptance pass
All source-defined alternatives and final beats remain in coverage, including excess or broken ones
No automatic retry or omitted-mode exemption
Build exclusions apply only to generated runtime cache/trace evidence, not application source

observationProblems: final beat count 10, normal scope 12 to 22
limits: Coordinator rules/code are frozen before actor; identities are source-bound observations after a real gate. Outside-workspace paths alone are not a write barrier.
Dependency entrypoint hashes are recorded, not full dependency integrity. The harness must audit dependency and lockfile mutation separately.
Next build executes application configuration. Fixed typecheck and lint commands use coordinator-generated configuration independently of actor scripts.
Headless Chromium viewport checks do not prove physical-phone performance, custom-object quality, truth of claims or external-link availability.
Screenshots require human visual review. Text and scene markers alone cannot establish faithful formations or visually correct 3D.
Control state/image changes and motion positions measure observable response, not whether the intended 3D component responded correctly.

exclusions: verified top-level hidden bare Git metadata trees (bounded layout and marker validation)

visualReview: unobserved: original pixels and semantic scene/control targets require separate review
